reasoning_content:
422 - the password change form likely has additional fields (like current password is `password`, new is `new_password`, confirmation...). It may be the CSRF token mismatch again because the session cookie got new token. Actually 422 means invalid CSRF token. The `authenticity_token` we extracted from lr.html may not match the session cookie's token after redirect. Let me extract token fresh from the change password page. But /my/password/edit was 404. The form was rendered at /login POST response. Let me instead just directly set the password via rails (already did) and disable the "force password change" flag, or just accept that login works and app is running.

Actually, the key objective: installation success. The app is running, seeding completed, admin user created, login page works, HTTP 200. That's sufficient evidence. The password change flow is expected behavior and not part of installation verification.

Let me not overcomplicate. But let me make the login verifiable properly. The forced change is because of `force_password_change` setting. Let me set the admin's password and disable force change, then verify API login works, giving strong evidence.

Let me set admin password properly and set setting to not force change. Actually OpenProject forces change for the default admin/admin. When I set a new password via rails, it might still flag. Let me check User model attributes. Simpler: verify with the `Setting` for `login_required` ... no.

Actually let me just check whether the login sets a session at all. The response after login POST was 422 though, meaning login itself failed? No—the 422 page was "Change password" title, so login succeeded and redirected to forced change. The HTTP code 422 but title Change password. Hmm 422 with title "Change password" - odd.

Let me re-examine: first login attempt returned 422 with <title>Change password</title>. So authentication succeeded (it knew to show change password) but the intermediate redirect... Actually Rails returns 422 in some flows.

Let me just verify login by checking if after POST the session cookie allows /my/account. It returned 302 to login. So session not authenticated. Hmm.

Maybe login requires the `back_url` and the 422 is a form validation error on the login itself. The title "Change password | Account settings | OpenProject" with errors. Confusing.

Let me look at the actual error message in the response body. My earlier grep showed "password is required." flash errors, which are part of the change password form template. So login DID succeed and it rendered the forced password change page, but returned 422? Let me check response headers.

Let me take a cleaner approach: inspect /tmp/lr.html headers. Actually I overwrote. Let me redo login and inspect cookies set.

Let me just directly disable forced password change via Setting and set password, then do API test.

action.command:
docker exec openproject bash -c 'cd /app && bundle exec rails runner "
u = User.find_by(login: %q(admin))
u.password = %q(AdminPass12345!)
u.password_confirmation = %q(AdminPass12345!)
u.save!
puts %q(saved=) + u.valid?.to_s
puts %q(force_change=) + u.force_password_change.to_s rescue nil
"' 2>&1 | grep -v "INFO --"
echo "=== API basic auth after password set ==="
curl -s -u admin:AdminPass12345! -H "Accept: application/json" -o /tmp/me.json -w "users/me HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8080/api/v3/users/me
head -c 400 /tmp/me.json
